dashboard.title: System Overview
dashboard.description: Aeon Data Systems is a forensic recovery and secure data-destruction tool. Use The Hunter to scan a storage device for deleted or hidden files, and The Oblivion to permanently destroy sensitive data beyond recovery. Start by selecting a storage device from the left sidebar.
dashboard.startScanDesc: Recover deleted files via sector-level carving

hunter.title: The Hunter — Forensic Recovery
hunter.description: Reads the selected device sector by sector, searching for JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, ZIP, DOC, EXE, MP4, MP3, AVI, RAR and SQLite file signatures. Deleted or hidden files are listed below for recovery.
hunter.selectFirst: ← Select a device from the sidebar first.

oblivion.title: The Oblivion — Military-Grade Shredder
oblivion.description: Overwrites a file or entire drive with cryptographically random data using DoD 5220.22-M, Gutmann 35-pass, or NVMe hardware sanitize. Enter a file path or a device path (e.g. {{path}}).

DoD5220.name: DoD 5220.22-M
DoD5220.forWhom: Best for: files, USB drives, HDD disks
DoD5220.desc: 3 passes: zeros → ones → random. Official US Department of Defense standard (NISPOM). Works on HDDs and regular files. Balance of security and speed — takes a few minutes per GB.

Gutmann35.name: Gutmann 35-Pass
Gutmann35.forWhom: Best for: old HDDs with sensitive data. NOT for SSDs.
Gutmann35.desc: 35 passes based on Peter Gutmann's 1996 paper targeting magnetic encoding residues on older HDD platters. The extra patterns are unnecessary on modern HDDs and useless on SSDs, but provide maximum psychological assurance. Expect hours per GB.

RandomSingle.name: Random (1-Pass)
RandomSingle.recommendation: ⚡ Best for SSDs and quick file deletion
RandomSingle.forWhom: Best for: SSDs, NVMe, USB flash, individual files
RandomSingle.desc: Single pass of cryptographically strong random data (ChaCha20 CSPRNG). Modern research shows one random pass is sufficient to prevent recovery on SSDs and flash storage. Fastest option — typically seconds to minutes per GB.

NvmeSanitize.name: NVMe Sanitize
NvmeSanitize.forWhom: Best for: NVMe SSDs, M.2 drives — full drive only
NvmeSanitize.desc: Sends a hardware Sanitize command directly to the NVMe controller. The drive's firmware erases every NAND flash block — including wear-leveling reserves invisible to software. This is the most thorough method for SSDs. Requires administrator and a device path like \.\PhysicalDrive0.

NvmeFormat.name: NVMe Format NVM
NvmeFormat.recommendation: 🔧 Alternative to Sanitize on some NVMe drives
NvmeFormat.forWhom: Best for: NVMe drives where Sanitize is not supported
NvmeFormat.desc: Issues the NVMe Format NVM command (User Data Erase) to the controller, resetting the drive namespace. Faster than Sanitize on some controllers, slightly less thorough. Also requires administrator and a raw device path.

shred.targetLabel: Target — file path or device path
shred.browseTitle: Select file or drive to shred
shred.fileHelp: For a <1>file</1>: enter the full path (e.g. <2>F:\secret.docx</2>). The file will be overwritten and then <1>deleted</1>.
shred.driveHelp: For an <1>entire drive</1>: use a device path like <2>\\.\C:</2> or <2>\\.\PhysicalDrive0</2> (requires administrator).

warning.title: IRREVERSIBLE ACTION
warning.body: All data at <1>{{path}}</1> will be permanently destroyed using <2>{{algo}}</2>. This cannot be undone.
warning.confirm: I confirm this data will be permanently destroyed

complete.title: Destruction complete.
complete.body: All passes finished. For files: content overwritten and file deleted. Data is unrecoverable.

error.title: Shred operation failed
error.hint: Common causes: path does not exist, insufficient permissions (run as administrator for device paths), or the drive is in use.
